title: Senior Control Systems Engineer – Vehicle Dynamics & Abstraction (m/f/d)
description:
We are seeking a Senior Control Systems Engineer to lead the design and execution of robust control layers across a highly diverse fleet of autonomous vehicles. In this role, you will act as the critical boundary layer to the upper autonomy stack. As the industry transitions toward End-to-End driving models, your primary mandate is to ensure that high-level motion commands are executed sensibly and strictly safeguarded at the physical limits of the vehicle.

Your designs will address complex, real-world scenarios rather than idealized environments. You will build control architectures that remain robust under severe, highly non-linear real-world conditions. This includes handling sudden tire slip, navigating challenging terrain such as mud, gravel, potholes, and dense vegetation, maintaining stability on steep inclines and side slopes, and delivering predictable tracking despite asymmetric system degradation, such as a damaged mechanics.

What is your Day to Day Mission:

- Control Architecture Abstraction: Maintain a standardized, platform-agnostic motion command interface that cleanly abstracts underlying mechanical complexity from the planning layers.

- Multivariable Control & Allocation: Design and deploy control laws to manage path tracking, velocity execution, and actuator saturation, incorporating data-driven control allocation to dynamically distribute effort across multiple actuators.

- System Identification & Modeling: Utilize data-driven system identification techniques to model unknown plant dynamics, latencies, and actuator responses.

- Pragmatic Simulation & Verification: Validate control loops rapidly. If filter design and linear/nonlinear analysis indicate a controller will behave, you are empowered to rely on lean, pragmatic subsystem simulations to iterate fast rather than being bottlenecked waiting for massive, full-system high-fidelity simulation runs.

- Motion Safeguarding: Ensure that incoming motion commands are dynamically evaluated, bounded, and safeguarded against the physical realities and constraints of the vehicle chassis in real time.

What you bring to the team:

- Experience: Proven professional experience developing and deploying real-time closed-loop control systems.

- Linear & Classical Control Design: Deep foundational command of classical control theory, including frequency-domain loop-shaping, stability margin analysis (Bode/Nyquist), and standard state-space design methods (LQR/pole-placement).

- System Identification & Allocation: Demonstrated experience utilizing system identification methods or empirical frequency response estimation to characterize raw plant dynamics, alongside data-driven control allocation techniques.

- Nonlinear Control Theory: Strong theoretical and practical foundation in Differential Geometry as applied to nonlinear systems, specifically utilizing Feedback Linearization and Differential Flatness for exact state transformation.

- State Estimation: Proficiency in Kalman Filtering for state estimation under non-holonomic constraints.

- Implementation & Tooling: High proficiency in either the MATLAB/Simulink, C++, or Python. The core requirement is your ability to translate complex control logic into clean, deterministic execution ready for real-time environments.

Your Benefits:

- Direct impact: See your contributions rapidly integrated from cutting-edge research into industrialized products, flying in the field within short development cycles.

- Culture & Environment: A dynamic, fast-paced, and collaborative startup environment with flat hierarchies, efficient collaboration, and a strong emphasis on continuous learning opportunities.

- Work-life Balance: We offer flexible work schedules, and 30 days of paid vacation each year to support your personal and professional life.

- Lunch Benefit: We promote healthy eating and the well-being of our employees with a monthly lunch budget.

- Health & Wellness: We support your physical well-being with a company-subsidized eGym Wellpass membership, giving you access to thousands of gyms and sports facilities.

description:

Tenable® is the Exposure Management company. Over 40,000 organizations around the globe rely on Tenable to understand and reduce cyber risk. Our global employees support 65 percent of the Fortune 500, 50 percent of the Global 2000, and large government agencies. Come be part of our journey!

Ask a member of our team and they’ll answer, “Our people!” We work together to build and innovate best-in-class cybersecurity solutions for our customers; all while creating a culture of belonging, respect, and excellence where we can be our best selves. When you’re part of our #OneTenable team, you can expect to partner with some of the most talented and passionate people in the industry, and have the support and resources you need to do work that truly matters. We deliver results that exceed expectations and we win together!

You have built a career carrying a number, and now you want to grow big accounts for the long term. This role is for you. You will own renewals and expansion for 30 to 40 of Tenable's strategic customers, including the largest account in EMEA. Retention and growth in these accounts is now a top priority, so your impact will be visible fast. You will be in front of customers and in the room with senior leaders, working side by side with our Enterprise and Commercial Territory Managers and Solutions Engineers as an equal. This is a sales role with a Customer Success title.

Your mandate is to keep our largest customers and grow them. You will protect recurring revenue, find the next opportunity in every account, and set the standard for what a Principal CSM looks like at Tenable. Keep our biggest customers, and keep them growing strategic customers stay when they see the value. You will make it clear, and make it last.

  • Own the full renewal cycle for a multi-million book, with retention as your first measure.

  • Spot churn and downgrade risk early, using adoption data and your own judgement.

  • Negotiate enterprise contracts that protect revenue and open the door to more.

Turn every account into the next big deal, renewals and expansion are an equal share of the role.

  • Run strategic discovery with senior stakeholders to uncover high-value opportunities.

  • Build the business case for upsell and cross-sell across the Tenable platform.

  • Plan each account together with Territory Managers and Solutions Engineers.

  • Lead critical escalations, and bring in Engineering, Support and Professional Services at pace.

  • Share what you hear from customers, so it shapes our product and service.

Shape what Principal means, this is still a new level for us, and you will help define it.

  • Set the playbook for renewals and expansion in strategic accounts.

  • Mentor junior and senior CSMs, and show them what great looks like.

  • Build the experience and profile that opens a path to team leadership.

What success looks like

  • By six months: a plan and a trusted forecast for every strategic account, and a senior contact in each one.

  • By twelve months: retention ahead of baseline, double-digit growth in your book, and a team that looks to you for best practice.

  • Experience of large, complex accounts and enterprise contract negotiation, ideally using a structured method such as MEDDPICC.

description:
At Abnormal AI, we protect our customers against nefarious adversaries who are constantly evolving their techniques and tactics to outwit and undermine the traditional approaches to Security.

About The Team

This team owns the end-to-end development and operation of the infrastructure, ML models, AI agents, customer-facing APIs, and internal tools that power Abnormal's Identity Threat Protection (ITP) product. Our work is central to detecting malicious behavior and protecting customers from advanced identity-based attacks — including account takeover, identity spoofing, data leakage, and other high-impact threats.

About The Role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to help build and evolve our platform as it scales to meet expanding product requirements. This role blends hands-on backend systems development with growing ownership of features and production systems, including AI-powered and agentic components, working closely with senior engineers to improve system reliability, reduce latency, and accelerate feature release cycles.

What You'll Do

Technical Delivery & Excellence

  • Design, build, and iterate on scalable backend and ML systems, APIs, frameworks, and internal tools.
  • Take ownership of well-scoped features and components, with guidance from senior engineers on more complex, cross-system work.
  • Contribute to the stability, reliability, and operational excellence of critical systems.
  • Write clean, testable, and resilient code with attention to edge cases and performance.
  • Contribute to technical design documents and participate in design discussions.
  • Participate in code and design reviews, and contribute to on-call rotations.

AI Engineering & Agents

  • Help design and build LLM-powered features and agentic workflows (e.g., automated investigation, triage, or remediation assistants) as part of the ATO platform.
  • Integrate LLM APIs and agent frameworks into backend services, with attention to reliability, cost, latency, and evaluation.
  • Contribute to prompt design, tool/function-calling integrations, and guardrails for AI-driven components under senior engineer guidance.
  • Use GenAI coding assistants and agents as part of your own development workflow to accelerate delivery and testing.

Collaboration & Growth

  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, and engineers to align on specifications and priorities.
  • Break down well-defined projects into clear executable steps and drive them to completion.
  • Contribute to roadmap discussions and share ideas for technical improvements.
  • Communicate effectively in an async-first environment, providing clarity on updates, challenges, and solutions.
  • Actively seek feedback and mentorship from senior engineers to accelerate your growth.

What We're Looking For

  • Ownership & Growth: A proactive engineer who takes ownership of assigned work and is eager to grow into increasingly complex projects.
  • Attention to Detail: Strong focus on code quality, reliability, monitoring, and performance.
  • Solid Fundamentals: Good grounding in system design principles, with a growing ability to reason about scaling and reliability tradeoffs.
  • Strong Collaborator: Comfortable working cross-functionally and in a distributed environment.
  • AI & Agent Engineering Curiosity: Genuine interest in LLM-powered features and agentic systems, and proactive in leveraging modern developer productivity tools, including GenAI assistants and coding agents, to accelerate delivery.

Must-Have Skills

  • 3-5 years of industry experience as a Software Engineer, with a track record of shipping production backend systems.
  • Solid backend proficiency in Python, with experience building and maintaining production systems.
  • Experience with system design fundamentals and building reliable, scalable applications.
  • Working knowledge of relational databases and modern data storage technologies.
  • Exposure to service-to-service communication (gRPC, Kafka) and caching (Redis) is a plus.
  • Experience with AWS cloud services (S3, RDS) and deployment practices.
  • Familiarity with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, Helm) is a plus.
  • Understanding of service health, monitoring, and incident response practices.
  • Comfortable writing technical documentation and contributing to design discussions.

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) into production applications.
  • Exposure to agent frameworks or patterns (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, tool/function calling, ReAct-style agents).
  • Familiarity with prompt engineering, evaluation, and observability for AI-driven features.

title: Software Engineer, General - London
description:
About InstaLILY

InstaLILY is an AI products and infrastructure company that puts execution at the frontier of enterprise AI. That work begins with Lily™, the world's first AI Forward Deployed Engineer, which learns how a business works, builds the software it needs, and goes live in days. It does not leave when the work ships; it stays and keeps the software working as the business changes. Lily runs wherever the work happens, in the cloud, on-premise, or at the edge, through InstaLILY's Small Data Center, built with NVIDIA technology. Founded in 2023 by Amit Shah and Sumantro Das, InstaLILY has raised nearly $100 million from Energize Capital, Insight Partners, and Home Depot Ventures. Headquartered in New York, with offices in San Francisco, London, and Toronto, InstaLILY serves leading companies across construction, industrial distribution, logistics, healthcare, and other operationally intensive industries. Learn more at https://instalily.ai/.

The Traction

Revenue grew 5x over the past year, and Lily has driven over $200M in new annual sales for a single customer. We serve some of the largest operators in our industries, including SRS Distribution (part of The Home Depot family), United Rentals, and Henry Schein, and we work closely with the Google DeepMind and NVIDIA ecosystems.

How We Work

We work in small teams with real ownership: clear problems, direct access to the customers whose work you're changing, and room to ship. Your code runs in live production systems inside billion-dollar operations, so you see your impact directly. People who do well here want that proximity to the work. We're growing fast, and the people who join now shape what this company becomes. Everything runs on three principles: Customers, Culture, and Code.

Responsibilities

  • Continue to develop the core AI platform and drive technical excellence throughout the organization.
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams (product, UI/UX, business development) to design and implement new features and capabilities.
  • Rapidly learn into the expected quality and reliability of the platform through comprehensive testing and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) practices.
  • Build a rapport with the Lead Software Engineer and Head of Product while fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
  • Collaborate with the product and design teams to deliver high-quality products that meet customer needs.
  • Stay up-to-date with the latest AI and software engineering trends and technologies.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, Mathematics, Physics or a related field.
  • First Class degree preferred.
  • 0 to 2 years of experience as a software engineer (prior software engineering internships and experience/projects a significant plus).
  • Passion for understanding AI and machine learning technologies.
  • Experience with Python, JavaScript, and other programming languages.
  • Understanding of cloud computing technologies OR experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Track record of delivering successful products / working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment is a plus.

What You'll Get

  • Real traction: The product works, customers are live, and we've already driven over $200M in incremental revenue for customers — this isn't a bet on an unproven thesis.
  • Deep partnerships: Backed by Insight Partners with deep ecosystem partnerships across Google, NVIDIA, and Microsoft. InstaLILY's architecture has been featured in Google DeepMind's case study showcase.
  • Customer impact: You'll drive measurable operational change inside the customers you own.
  • Stage: Early enough to shape how InstaLILY runs customer relationships and expansion at scale.
  • Culture: Offices in New York, San Francisco, and London — sharp, low-ego team moving fast.

title: Senior AI Engineer (GTM)
description:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.

The role:

We’re looking for an entrepreneurial and technically strong Senior AI Engineer to join our Data & AI team and work with our Go-To-Market organisation.

This is a builder's role, end to end. You’ll work closely with Marketing, Sales, and RevOps to solve high-value problems, design practical AI solutions and build them into reliable systems that people use every day. You’ll be expected to move comfortably from an ambiguous business challenge to a technical design, a working prototype, and then a production-ready solution.

Your work could include building systems that segment and prioritise accounts, developing agents that automate sales workflows, or creating intelligent tools that help our teams research prospects and act on buying signals. You’ll own the full lifecycle of what you build, including evaluation, observability, reliability and cost optimisation.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys being close to users, can write production-quality code and is excited by the challenge of turning rapidly evolving AI capabilities into valuable commercial outcomes. Experience working with GTM teams is useful, but the ability to understand problems, build effective systems and measure their impact is more important.

What you'll do:

- Design and build AI-powered systems for account segmentation, enrichment, scoring, prioritisation and buying-signal detection

- Develop and deploy agentic workflows for use cases such as account research, outbound personalisation, call summarisation and CRM hygiene

- Write production-quality code and build the integrations, data pipelines and services required to take solutions from prototype to reliable daily use

- Optimise systems for quality, latency and cost through evaluation, prompt design, model selection, routing, caching, context management and token optimisation

- Establish practical patterns for building AI systems at Paddle, including monitoring, guardrails, documentation and clear measures of business impact

We'd love to hear from you if you:

- Have strong software engineering experience and can independently take a problem from technical design through to production; Python and SQL experience would be particularly relevant

- Have hands-on experience building applications with large language models, APIs, retrieval systems, agents or other applied AI technologies

- Understand how to evaluate and operate AI systems in production, including managing hallucination risk, latency, reliability, context limits and variable model costs

- Are comfortable working with structured and unstructured data, building integrations and turning information from multiple sources into useful systems

- Have an interest in commercial problems and can understand concepts such as ICP, segmentation, pipeline, buyer intent and sales workflows; direct GTM experience is beneficial but not essential

- Enjoy working directly with the people who use what you build, are comfortable with ambiguity and can balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

- Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

- Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

- Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

Connecting at Paddle

We’re a ‘digital-first’ company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

Our Paddle hubs:

- In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)

- In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)

- In APAC: Singapore

Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work.

To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description.

Compensation: CA$0 – CA$150K

- • For this role, the expected base salary range is circa CA$0 – CA$150K

title: Head of Data Science
description:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.

The role:

We are looking for a Head of Data Science to build Paddle's data science capability from the ground up. Our Merchant of Record model gives us a data position no PSP or billing provider has: subscription and pricing context alongside granular payment-outcome data, across thousands of software businesses. This role exists to turn that into economic value by putting machine learning and agentic systems into production.

The mandate is deliberately narrow and deliberately ambitious: data science at Paddle owns automated decisioning inside the product — traditional machine learning and agentic systems alike — not decision-support analytics.

We have a long list of candidate opportunities than we can fund, spanning payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance. We have a working hypothesis about which of these pays back first, and we'll share it — but part of the job in your first quarter is to pressure-test it, size the alternatives yourself, and tell us where to start.

This is a founding role, and for the first few quarters it is a building role more than a managing one. You'll be the only person in the function: doing the analysis, engineering the features, training and evaluating the models or agents, taking the first system live with our engineering teams — and then operating it, answerable for its uptime, its drift and its numbers. Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance.

What you'll do:

- Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly.

- Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build.

- Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them.

- Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way.

- Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on.

- Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed.

- Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value.

- Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design.

- Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous.

- Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall.

We'd love to hear from you if you:

- Experienced leading data science or ML teams that own systems in production, with deployments that moved a commercial metric and kept running afterwards. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for.

- Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's.

- Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other.

- Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on.

- Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep.

- Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience.

- Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise.

- Fluent in the engineering side of production ML and agents (training pipelines, model registries, inference services, feature stores, drift detection, trace observability) and able to hold your own with senior engineers on latency, availability, observability and rollback.

- Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet.

- Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work.

- Experienced in payments, fintech, subscriptions, high-volume commercial operations or another regulated transactional domain — enough to get to a credible value estimate in a new area quickly.

- Comfortable treating regulated ML as a design constraint rather than paperwork — model risk assessment, DPIAs, auditability, traceability of model and policy versions to production decision logic.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance.

What you'll do: 

  • Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly.

  • Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build.

  • Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them.

  • Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way.

  • Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on.

  • Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed.

  • Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value.

  • Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design.

  • Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous.

  • Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall.

We'd love to hear from you if you:

  • Experienced leading data science or ML teams that own systems in production, with deployments that moved a commercial metric and kept running afterwards. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for.

  • Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's.

  • Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other.

  • Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on.

  • Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep.

  • Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience.

  • Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise.

  • Fluent in the engineering side of production ML and agents (training pipelines, model registries, inference services, feature stores, drift detection, trace observability) and able to hold your own with senior engineers on latency, availability, observability and rollback.

  • Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet.

  • Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work.

  • Experienced in payments, fintech, subscriptions, high-volume commercial operations or another regulated transactional domain — enough to get to a credible value estimate in a new area quickly.

  • Comfortable treating regulated ML as a design constraint rather than paperwork — model risk assessment, DPIAs, auditability, traceability of model and policy versions to production decision logic.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.

 

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

  • Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

  • Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

  • Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

 

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

 

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

 

Connecting at Paddle

We’re a ‘digital-first’ company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

 

Our Paddle hubs:

  • In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)

  • In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)

  • In APAC: Singapore

Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work.

 

To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

About the Role

The Chief of Staff will drive major priorities across ActAI and its portfolio of businesses. This is a hands-on operating role for someone who can move across businesses and functions, solve difficult problems and drive important work from decision through execution.

What you will be doing

- Drive major Group priorities and cross-functional projects from start to completion.

- Identify business or execution problems, work through the details and drive solutions.

- Track priorities, decisions and performance across businesses and ensure clear ownership and follow-through.

- Lead projects involving new businesses, market expansion, organisational changes or other Group priorities.

- Analyse business performance, markets and opportunities and turn findings into actions.

- Work across product, technology, finance, people and operations depending on the problem.

- Step into areas where ownership is unclear or additional execution is needed.

What you will need

- Strong experience in a technology company, high-growth startup, strategy/operations role, top-tier consulting firm or your own startup.

- Track record owning complex projects with measurable business outcomes.

- Strong analytical and commercial judgement with the ability to work through data, financials and business problems.

- Able to learn unfamiliar businesses and functions quickly and get into the details.

- Strong written and verbal communication with clear, structured thinking.

- Hands-on operating style - able to do the analysis, build the plan and drive the execution personally.

title: Special Projects
description:
Special Projects

London (Shoreditch) | In person | Full time

About Seamflow

We're removing one of the last great barriers to progress in the physical world. While software moves fast, industries like healthcare, aerospace, and energy are still slowed by outdated, manual systems.

Our vision is to unlock enormous value for Testing, Inspection, and Certification companies globally. The market is vast, the problem is real, and we're just getting started.

We're rapidly growing following our 14x oversubscribed seed round backed by Tier 1 investors including Northzone and Initialized Capital. These funds backed the founders of Coinbase, Reddit, Klarna, and Spotify.

We're growing very fast; demand is outstripping our supply, and we're building fast to keep up.

The Team

Our team includes AI researchers from world-leading academic institutions like Johns Hopkins, MIPT, Oxford, Cambridge and UCL, former founding engineers at unicorn startups, and alumni of X, Google, Amazon, and Yandex, alongside former leaders from McKinsey, BCG and Bain. We look for people who move fast, think clearly, and hold themselves to a high bar. The standard here is very high, and we're looking for someone who raises it further.

The Role

Special Projects sits directly alongside the CEO and Chief of Staff and takes on whatever the company needs most at that moment. There is no fixed remit and there is no playbook.

One month that means preparing the material and the numbers behind a fundraise. The next it's working through legal, regulatory, and market access questions in a country we're entering, or holding an entire function open on your own until we've hired someone permanent into it. Whatever is broken, missing, or unowned lands here first.

Be clear eyed about what this is. It is demanding, and a lot of it is unglamorous. Some of it is detail work that simply has to be right, with nobody available to check it behind you. What we need is a workhorse who is obsessive about detail, who closes things out rather than hands them back, and whose work nobody ever has to second guess. If that reads as a description of you rather than a warning, this is the highest leverage seat in the company for someone early in their career. You will be in the room for decisions most people see five years later.

What We're Looking For

1–3 years in an environment with a high bar and short feedback loops: investment banking, strategy consulting, a fast growing startup, or something equally demanding we haven't thought of.

An exceptional track record: We care that you were at the top of whatever room you were in, academically and professionally.

AI-native: You already run your work through AI and operate at 10x as a result. You reach for these tools by default, not as a novelty, and you're constantly finding new ways to compress what used to take days into hours.

Structured thinking: You break messy, ambiguous problems into parts, work out what actually matters, and sequence it. You can explain your reasoning on a whiteboard in two minutes.

Ruthless organisation: Multiple workstreams, nothing dropped, nothing chased twice, everything written down.

Strong with Excel, slides, and written communication: Most of our work travels as documents and models read by executives at large regulated businesses.

Bias to action: You'd rather ship a good plan today than a perfect one next week.

Work nobody has to check: You close the loop, catch your own mistakes, and flag the things you couldn't resolve rather than leaving them to be discovered.

Low ego, high agency: The work ranges from a board memo to cleaning a customer data set at 9pm. Neither is beneath you, and you'll take on the boring half as readily as the interesting half.

Someone who wants to be in the room, not on a call. This role is in-person, full time at our Shoreditch office.

Nice to have: European languages, particularly German or French.

What You'll Get

A huge amount of responsibility and trust from day one, and direct exposure to every decision that shapes the company

A front row seat to enterprise sales, product, fundraising, and operations, and a real say in all of them

A clear path into an operating or commercial leadership role as we scale or insight into how to start your own tech company some day

A team that moves fast, works hard, and backs each other fully

Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access

title: Commercial Operations Associate
description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The team

Griffin is a UK bank built for builders. We give fintechs and platforms the bank accounts and payment rails to launch their own financial products, and clients like Uber, Yonder, Anna Money and Counting Up build on us. Our commercial team brings sales, customer success and marketing together to win, onboard and grow those clients. We’re a team of 10 people, made up of former founders and growth specialists.

The opportunity

You’ll become the engine behind how our commercial team makes decisions. Working alongside the Chief Revenue Officer, the Head of Commercial and the Head of Marketing, you’ll see the full picture of how a bank wins, onboards and grows its clients, and your analysis will shape where the team focuses next. There’s no narrow lane here. One week you’re building a forecast, the next you’re preparing a renewal review, and if something needs an owner, it’s yours.

What success looks like

In your first 6 months, you’ll have given the commercial team a forecast it trusts and spotted risks early, so every quarter end runs smoothly. People across Sales, Customer Success and Marketing will rely on our data because it’s accurate and up to date, and the team’s reviews will run like clockwork. The board and investors will receive numbers they can follow with confidence, and the executive team will already be turning to you for its priority projects.

To do this you’ll own

- The numbers: the reporting that runs our commercial business, from pipeline and bookings to annual recurring revenue (ARR), net revenue retention and consumption against forecast, plus pricing and deal-structure modelling, including consumption-based pricing and customer profitability

- Our CRM: clean, well-structured data, built with Sales and Customer Success around clear stage definitions and fields people actually use

- Sales and customer success insight: analysis of conversion, sales cycle length, win and loss reasons and pipeline coverage, plus account analysis for renewals covering volumes, revenue, margin and product adoption

- Marketing performance: campaign tracking and pipeline attribution so every pound of spend ties back to revenue, alongside ad hoc work like target account lists and event reporting

- Commercial governance: deal approval and discount policies, pricing and contract records and clear audit trails, working with Legal, Compliance and Finance

- Our operating cadence: documented processes and the weekly, monthly and quarterly reviews that keep the team in rhythm

- Executive projects: high-priority projects, briefings and materials that give you close exposure to how strategic decisions get made

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that’s for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To ensure this, we’re looking for people who have most of the following:

- You’ll have some experience as an operator. If it’s in a commercial, revenue operations, sales operations, analytics, consulting or finance role then that’s a bonus

- A habit of rolling up your sleeves and taking ownership without waiting to be asked

- Curiosity about fintech, banking and how money moves

- A structured mind and an eye for detail, with the flexibility to switch between spreadsheets, research and talking to people, and a knack for finding the story in the numbers and explaining it simply

- The ability to learn quickly, ask good questions and take feedback well

- A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

Ideally, you would also:

- Have experience in fintech, SaaS or a fast-growing startup

- Want to build a career in commercial, sales or growth

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We don’t work with recruitment agencies, so please don’t send us speculative CVs.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

title: Software Engineer (Frontend) - London
description:
About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We recently raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

title: Senior Manager External Reporting
description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About the Role

Volta is building AI-ready data centre infrastructure across the UK, Norway, Germany, Spain and the US, and is preparing for a US public listing following a Series A led by a16z and Altimeter. We will register on Form S-1 and report as a US domestic filer on Forms 10-K and 10-Q. Building the external reporting infrastructure - US GAAP consolidated financial statements, SEC-standard disclosures and a close process that can sustain a quarterly filing cadence - is one of Finance's defining projects over the next 12 to 16 months.

As Senior Manager, External Reporting you will own group consolidation and external reporting end to end: consolidating the group's UK, US and European entities, running the ASC 830 translation mechanics, preparing the US GAAP financial statements and footnotes, drafting the S-1 and the periodic filings that follow, and building the tie-out discipline expected of a registrant.

You will report to the VP Accounting and work alongside the Director of Technical Accounting, who owns accounting positions and policy. You will be central to S-1 preparation and to Volta's first audited financial statements.

This is a build role, and in the first year a hands-on one. There is no team beneath the role today. You will prepare the statements, write the footnotes and run the tie-out yourself, with support following as the function scales. If you are looking to direct the work rather than do it, this is not the right role.

The role is scoped to grow. As the reporting team builds beneath it and the filing cadence reaches steady state, we expect it to progress to Director.

What You Will Be Doing

- Own the group consolidation across the UK, US and European entities, including intercompany elimination and ASC 830 foreign currency translation

- Prepare US GAAP consolidated financial statements with full footnote disclosure, for audit and for filing

- Draft SEC disclosures to registrant standard - the S-1 financial statement sections, MD&A support under Reg S-K Item 303, and the 10-K and 10-Q filings that follow - working with the Director of Technical Accounting, the VP Accounting and the wider team

- Own the tie-out process: every number in the statements agreed to support, referenced and reviewable

- Build the disclosure checklist and the annual and quarterly reporting calendar from scratch, and design a close timetable that meets a 10-Q filing deadline

- Coordinate audit deliverables through first-year fieldwork and completion, and through the quarterly review cycles that follow

- Sign off the US GAAP group numbers that feed the statutory bridge, working alongside the Statutory Reporting Manager who prepares the local IFRS accounts

- Own the consolidated actuals that management and board reporting are built from, and review non-GAAP measures and their reconciliations

- Select and implement disclosure management and inline XBRL tagging, required from the S-1 onwards

- Support Reg S-X significance testing and Article 11 pro forma preparation as the site and joint venture portfolio develops

- Shape and, in time, lead the reporting team as the function scales

What You Bring

- Qualified accountant (ACA/CPA or equivalent) with 6 to 8+ years' experience, including preparing US GAAP consolidated financial statements and footnotes

- Hands-on experience drafting or auditing SEC filings (S-1, 10-K, 10-Q) - registrant side or Big Four

- Strong command of US GAAP disclosure requirements and of multi-entity, multi-currency group consolidation, including foreign currency translation under ASC 830

- Working knowledge of Reg S-K and Reg S-X

- Meticulous tie-out and documentation discipline

- Experience taking external auditors through a full year-end cycle, and ideally through quarterly reviews

- Proven ability to build a process from nothing rather than operate one that already exists

- Willingness to do the work personally before there is a team to delegate it to, and the judgement to know when to start building that team

- IPO readiness or first-time registrant experience an advantage

- Comfort with deadline pressure and shifting priorities in a pre-IPO environment

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing. Its measure of success is the customer lifetime value it adds between sign-up and first loan.

The team sets its own goals and direction. It brings together engineers, data scientists, and product and strategy people. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time.

You'll lead two engineers and report to the head of engineering for iwoca's customer journey, from first application to repeat lending.

The role

As the Tech Lead, you'll spend most of your time building. The team is moving its offer logic out of a legacy monolith into a new service. It's the biggest change in a decade to the system behind iwoca's lending decisions. The next phase is yours to lead.

- Autonomy and ownership. You'll shape what the team builds, decide how to build it, and own what goes live. You'll set its engineering roadmap, including what to pull out of the monolith, what to rewrite, and in what order.

- Technical complexity. You'll design the team's part of the new service, which turns models and rules into a lending decision and optimises each offer across amount, duration, fee, and interest rate. You'll keep it reliable in production, easy to change as the models evolve, and able to show how it reached each decision.

- Experimentation and learning. You'll build the systems that let data scientists test new models on live applications. Some experiments run for years, until each loan reaches the end of its term. You'll see the long-term results of the team's lending decisions.

- Influence. You'll get colleagues across iwoca behind technical work that competes with new features for time.

- Leadership and growth. You'll line-manage and coach the team's engineers, setting context and helping them own projects end to end. As the team grows, you'll decide the skills and make-up it needs, and hire the engineers to match.

The requirements

Essential:

- Technical leadership. You've led a team of engineers for at least two years, including line management, while still remaining hands on.

- Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You've designed, built, and run customer-facing backend systems in production.

- Commercial or product thinking. You take a business goal, get to the root of what's needed and why, and turn it into a technical plan. You can explain a trade-off in terms of what it means for customers and the business.

- AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to deliver engineering work you couldn't have done alone. You help your team do the same. You judge where it's useful. You check its output before it reaches production.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

- Lending or payments experience. You've worked in lending, payments, or another domain where engineering decisions carry financial risk.

- Experimentation. You've built systems that run controlled experiments, especially long-running ones.

- Legacy migration. You've moved business-critical logic out of a complex legacy monolith and kept everything that depends on it working.

- Working with data scientists. You've worked with data scientists from prototype to production, and know their work well enough to challenge it.

- Python stack. You've worked with Python, Django, and PostgreSQL.

- Frontend. You've built frontend features as well as backend services.

The salary

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £130,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

title: Partnerships Manager - M&A Platform
description:
The company

It's still difficult for business owners to sell their business, or buy others, in the sub-£10m enterprise value market. Information asymmetry, lack of knowledge and low transaction values make it hard, and most M&A firms shy away from the segment because they can't serve it profitably. A generation of owner-managers is approaching retirement, and most of them have no realistic route to a sale.

manda exists to fix that. We match buyers with sellers in the part of the market everyone else ignores, and we finance acquisitions ourselves so buyers arrive pre-qualified and often pre-financed. We've sold the first businesses, funded the first acquisition loans, and we're now opening the platform up beyond the businesses that already bank with us.

manda is part of iwoca, one of Europe's leading fintech lenders. Since 2012 iwoca has provided more than £4 billion in funding and its mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments. That backing is why we can serve this market where others can't: a deep footprint in the SME economy with 150,000+ UK customers, the data and infrastructure of an established lender, and the ability to build clean, automated processes instead of running an advisory firm on spreadsheets.

We’re looking for a Partnership Manager - manda (iwoca's M&A Platform)

We're looking for someone to build the introducer network that brings business owners to manda, iwoca's M&A platform. Accountants, solicitors, wealth managers and brokers meet an owner who is thinking about retiring long before we do. Your job is to make sure that when they do they think of us, and that referring us is the easiest thing they do that day.

The role

Your mission is to build a referral channel that produces a steady flow of business owners who are genuinely ready to sell.

Today almost all of our sellers come from iwoca's own customer base, found by hand and worked one at a time. That works, but the pool is finite. The professionals who already advise business owners are the most credible route to the ones we'd otherwise never reach, and right now we have no systematic way of working with them.

You'll be starting from close to nothing, so the first version of this channel is yours to design. It also means the job is as much about making referrals actually arrive as it is about signing partners up.

It also has to scale. In this industry most partner flow still depends on people turning up at industry events, which works but stops the moment you stop showing up. We're after the version of this channel where referring a client to manda takes a couple of clicks inside the software an adviser already uses.

Key responsibilities include:

Build the introducer network

- Find and win the firms worth working with: accountancy practices, corporate finance boutiques, solicitors, wealth managers and business transfer agents. Work out which kinds of firm actually refer, and concentrate there.

- Do the outbound yourself. Identify the firm, get the meeting, make the case, and follow up until something happens.

- Design what we offer them: how a referral is made, what the partner gets, what we commit to in return, and how we keep them informed once their client is with us.

Make referrals actually arrive

- A signed partnership is worth nothing until a referral comes through. You'll own the ongoing relationship work that turns agreements into a flow: regular contact, keeping manda front of mind, briefing partner teams, and being the person they call.

- Track referral volume and quality by partner, and be honest about which relationships aren't working so we can stop spending time on them.

Make the channel scale

- Judge every partnership by whether it adds referrals without adding work. A relationship that only produces when you're in the room isn't a channel yet.

- Work out which partner technology is worth plugging into: the practice management and accounting software advisers already work in, tracked referral links and partner portals, and integrations that let a firm refer a client without leaving their own tools. You won't build these yourself, but you'll identify them, make the commercial case, and scope them with our Product Builder.

- Look for partners who can bring a book rather than one client at a time. One firm with hundreds of owner-managed clients is worth more to us than ten firms with five, if we can find a way to surface the right candidates across the whole book.

Work iwoca's existing network

- iwoca already has a broker network and a partnerships function with relationships across the SME economy. Working out where manda fits into those relationships is far faster than starting cold, and it's the first place to look.

Events and community

- Build a focused programme of events worth attending and, where it makes sense, running our own: succession and exit planning, accountancy and adviser events, industry gatherings, and business owner peer communities.

- Judge them on referrals rather than attendance, and stop going to the ones that don't produce. Events are how you find and land partners, not how the channel scales.

Prove the channel pays

- Establish what a referral actually costs us once your time, any partner incentives and events are counted, and how many convert into a signed mandate. We have an assumption in our financial model and nobody has yet tested it.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Essential:

- Around 4+ years in partnerships, channel or business development, ideally B2B, where you built or substantially grew a referral channel rather than inheriting one that already worked.

- You've done the full cycle yourself: identified the target firms, got the meetings, agreed the terms, and then managed the relationship afterwards.

- A background in M&A, marketplaces, business broking or business transfer.

- You understand that the work starts after the agreement is signed, and you have the discipline to keep a channel warm over months rather than weeks.

- Numerate and honest about performance. You track referrals by partner, you know which relationships are producing, and you say so when one isn't.

- You think in systems as well as relationships. You can tell the difference between a partnership that scales and one that only works while you're pushing it, and you'd rather replace your own manual work with an integration than defend it.

- Comfortable specifying technology without building it. You can look at a partner's tools and our product, work out what would make us the path of least resistance, and scope it clearly enough for a product team to build.

- Genuinely hands-on. There's no team to delegate to: you'll build the target list, send the emails, run the meetings and keep the CRM straight yourself.

- A commercial thinker with a bias for action, comfortable navigating ambiguity in an early-stage venture.

Bonus:

- Experience with accountancy, legal or wealth management channels specifically.

- Experience running an event programme with commercial targets attached to it.

- Familiarity with the UK succession and exit planning landscape.

- Comfortable treating a CRM as a discipline rather than an afterthought, ideally HubSpot.

- You've shipped a partner integration, an embedded referral flow or a software marketplace listing, or worked closely with a product team on one.

- Familiar with the software UK accountancy practices and advisers actually work in, such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, IRIS or Dext.

The salary

We expect to pay £55,000–£80,000 and an annual performance based bonus for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

- Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

- Flexible working hours.

- Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

- A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

- A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

- 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

- A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

- Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

- 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

- An employee equity incentive scheme.

- Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

- Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

- Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

- A learning and development budget for everyone.

- Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

- Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours.

The role

As a Senior Data Scientist in Credit Risk Modelling, you'll own credit risk and CLtV projects end to end – from spotting where the models hold the business back to getting the change live. - Causal estimation of offer terms. Estimating the causal effect of amount, duration, and price on customer outcomes.

- Unifying automated and manual models. Finding a principled way to put the two model families, which optimise slightly different objectives, on a common cost function.

- IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require.

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join the Direct Acquisition team.

Direct Acquisition includes iwoca's Marketing, Sales, Brand and Acquisition Tech teams. Together, they reach UK businesses of all shapes and sizes through paid and organic marketing channels and direct sales.

A new team in Direct Acquisition builds agents that automate and improve acquisition processes. That's its only focus, and it works closely with Acquisition Tech. It's small – a product owner and you – and everyone builds. You'll report to the Head of Direct Acquisition, who sets the commercial direction.

The role

As the Applied AI Engineer, you'll build the agents and the systems around them. Most of the work is system design and backend engineering.

You'll start with direct mail. The first goal is an agent that plans each monthly round, uses iwoca's existing predictive models to build the mailing file, and learns from the results as they come in. The pattern is simple to say and hard to get right: the agent orchestrates, deterministic code does the work, and a human in the loop approves the file before it goes to print. You'll work with the people who run each process to understand the edge cases, and with Core Systems and Compliance on access and controls.

The agents don't exist yet, and much is still open: which processes the team takes on, and what the architecture looks like. You'll own those design decisions and write most of the code yourself, much of it with AI coding tools. Some of this won't work, and finding out why is one of the main outputs of the role.

- Architecture. You'll design what agents need to run reliably: memory that persists between runs, task management, access to tools, permissions, and a record of every decision and why. You'll build each piece so the next process can reuse it.

- Guardrails. You'll decide where the agent uses judgement and where code enforces rules the agent can't change, like suppressions, compliance checks and budget limits.

- Delivery. You'll own each agent end to end: connect it to iwoca's predictive models, data pipelines and channel tools, and run it alongside the current process until it has shown it works.

- Measurement. You'll track how often agents need a person, where they fail, what they cost, and what they're worth.

The requirements

We're looking for the depth of someone who has solved hard problems, and the pace of someone who moves fast in areas that are new to them.

Essential:

- System ownership. You've owned a complex system end to end, from design to running it in production, and lived with the consequences of your architecture choices.

- Design judgement. You've made architecture decisions other people built on, and you can explain the trade-offs and what you'd change. When an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

- Pace. You've got things live quickly in unfamiliar areas and they kept working once people relied on them.

- Agent engineering. You've built systems where LLMs take actions – more than chat or summaries – and you can explain what went wrong and how you fixed it. You know when a problem needs an agent and when it needs a for-loop.

- Controls. You've built permissions, data access rules and audit trails into systems from the start.

- Constructive challenge. You work well with commercial and product colleagues, and when an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.

- AI leverage. You've used AI coding tools to produce engineering work you couldn't have delivered without them – a service, an integration, or an internal tool others use. You have opinions on how to get the most out of them, and you check their output before it reaches production.

- Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

- Languages and data tools. You've worked with Python, Go, Snowflake or dbt.

- Evaluation. You've built evals that measure how an agent performs and where it fails.

- Marketing and growth tech. You've worked with ad platforms, CRMs or direct mail.

- Quantitative foundations. You come from a numerical or technical field, such as physics, engineering, maths or computer science.

- Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.
